S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

info.persona: Vilma Garcia blends disciplined technical mastery with a solitary, routine‑driven lifestyle, channeling heritage through meticulous gardening, cooking, and culturally rich storytelling while quietly pursuing leadership and mentorship in a competitive industry.
info.professional_persona: Vilma Garcia, an exacting television and film camera operator and editor, they command ARRI Alexa and RED cameras with regimented lighting setups and precise post‑production workflows, preferring solo shoots and tight deadlines while quietly advancing toward a senior director of photography role and planning a boutique studio for documentaries that honor heritage traditions.
info.cultural_background: Vilma is a first‑generation Mexican‑American who grew up in a bilingual household in Southern California. Her family celebrates Día de los Muertos, Mexican Independence Day, and other cultural traditions, which have instilled in her a deep respect for community and heritage. Fluent in both Spanish and English, she often incorporates subtle cultural references into her work, such as framing shots that highlight Mexican architecture or using music cues that echo traditional rhythms. Although she has never married, her strong family ties and cultural values shape her identity, providing both a sense of belonging and a drive to represent her heritage responsibly in the media landscape.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Vilma finds solace in solitary, structured activities that complement her professional discipline. She tends a small vegetable garden in her backyard, cherishing the routine of planting, pruning, and harvesting. Cooking traditional Mexican meals—especially tamales, pozole, and mole—provides a creative outlet that connects her to her cultural roots. She enjoys reading historical nonfiction and classic literature, often keeping detailed notes in a bullet‑journal. On quiet evenings she practices calligraphy and listens to vintage mariachi recordings, while occasional solo trips to film festivals allow her to study emerging visual trends without the pressure of networking.
info.sports_persona: Vilma Garcia, a solitary early‑morning runner who tracks mileage in a bullet‑journal, they root for the Los Angeles Dodgers and Lakers while joining a low‑key women’s cycling group on Sundays to maintain a disciplined fitness regimen.
info.arts_persona: Vilma Garcia, a quiet devotee of classic literature and vintage mariachi recordings, they spend evenings perfecting calligraphy, draw visual inspiration from the stark cinematography of Orson Welles, and curate an indie documentary collection discovered at film festivals.
info.travel_persona: Vilma Garcia, an organized solo traveler, they schedule annual trips to Cannes and Berlin film festivals, budget weekend retreats to the historic adobe towns of New Mexico and the rugged trails of Big Sur, and favor meticulously planned itineraries over spontaneous wanderings.
info.culinary_persona: Vilma Garcia, an adept home chef, they spend weekends perfecting tamales, simmering pozole with hominy and smoked pork, and slow‑cooking mole with dried chilies, cacao, and spices, all logged in a bullet‑journal, while occasionally treating themselves to a late‑night taco stand after a long shoot.

info.persona: Hakim Smith is a mechanically precise production veteran with a restless artistic soul, whose love of vinyl, street photography, and mindfulness battles against chronic anxiety and a habit of impulsive spending.
info.professional_persona: Hakim Smith leverages over a decade of hands‑on production floor expertise in assembly line operations, machinery maintenance, and quality inspection to mentor coworkers while channeling their spontaneous, art‑infused problem‑solving mindset into a push for CNC certification and a vision of redesigning workplace signage with bold visual elements, all while using mindfulness practices to temper their intense emotional reactivity in high‑pressure supervisory roles.
info.cultural_background: Hakim identifies as African‑American and grew up in a close‑knit South‑Los Angeles neighborhood that celebrated Black cultural traditions, from the rhythmic beats of West Coast hip‑hop to the storytelling of spoken‑word poetry. His family’s roots trace back to the Great Migration, with grandparents who moved from the Southern United States seeking better opportunities. This heritage has instilled a strong sense of resilience, community solidarity, and pride in Black artistic expression. He regularly participates in local cultural events such as Kwanzaa celebrations, Black History Month panel discussions, and neighborhood block parties featuring live music and dance. While he values the broader multicultural tapestry of Los Angeles—including influences from Caribbean and West African diasporas—Hakim maintains a personal connection to the African‑American church community, where he finds both spiritual support and a platform for communal service.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime, Hakim immerses himself in Los Angeles’ vibrant visual arts scene, often wandering the city’s mural‑rich neighborhoods to practice street photography and capture the evolving urban canvas. He enjoys attending intimate gallery openings and community art workshops, where he can discuss new ideas with a few close friends. Music is a cornerstone of his leisure—he collects vinyl records, especially jazz, funk, and classic hip‑hop, and occasionally dabbles on an acoustic guitar. He also finds solace in cooking soul‑food meals with his family, tending a modest backyard garden, and practicing mindfulness meditation to manage his emotional reactivity. Reading speculative fiction and philosophy provides him intellectual stimulation and fuels his unconventional thinking.
info.sports_persona: Hakim Smith maintains a modest fitness regimen that includes early morning jogs through Griffith Park, weekend pickup basketball games with the local LA City Parks Rec league, occasional yoga sessions to calm anxiety, and they fervently follow the Los Angeles Lakers and Clippers while cheering on the LA Galaxy during the soccer season.
info.arts_persona: Hakim Smith immerses themselves in Los Angeles’s mural‑rich neighborhoods, capturing street art with a vintage Nikon, curates a private vinyl collection featuring Miles Davis, Parliament‑Funkadelic, and A Tribe Called Quest, and regularly attends intimate gallery openings spotlighting contemporary creators like Kehinde Wiley and Banksy, finding inspiration that fuels both their photography and workplace design ideas.
info.travel_persona: Hakim Smith embraces spontaneous, low‑key travel by jet‑setting to cultural hubs such as New Orleans for live jazz, Oaxaca for vibrant markets, and Berlin for its street‑art scene, while also taking weekend road trips to Joshua Tree and Santa Barbara, preferring Airbnb stays that allow meditation spaces and often planning trips on a whim despite a modest travel budget.
info.culinary_persona: Hakim Smith enjoys cooking soul‑food classics like smoked collard greens, buttery fried chicken, and spicy jambalaya seasoned with paprika and thyme, often incorporating fresh vegetables from their backyard garden and pairing meals with a curated selection of vintage vinyl, while they modestly rate themselves as an enthusiastic home chef who occasionally over‑spice dishes in an effort to perfect flavor depth.

info.persona: Isabella Saldana blends analytical rigor with artistic curiosity, channeling competitive drive into meticulous procurement, cautious finance, proactive health routines, selective sport pursuits, and vibrant creative hobbies, all while wrestling with a tendency toward worry and a love for solitary moments.
info.professional_persona: Isabella Saldana is a senior procurement strategist who leverages two decades of data-driven sourcing and contract negotiation expertise to steer cross-functional sourcing teams, while infusing an artist's eye for visual appeal into product selection and demanding rigorous KPI tracking that reflects their disciplined, competitive nature.
info.cultural_background: Isabella was raised in a Mexican-American household in Texas, where Spanish was spoken daily and traditional celebrations such as Dia de los Muertos and quinceaneras were central to family life. Her parents instilled a respect for Mexican craftsmanship, which influences her aesthetic sense and procurement choices. Bilingual and bicultural, she balances the communal values of her heritage with the individualistic, achievement-driven culture of her professional environment. She regularly participates in the local Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, supports community festivals, and maintains strong ties to her extended family in Mexico, bringing a blend of Mexican warmth and disciplined professionalism to all aspects of her life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Isabella's curiosity drives her to explore visual arts; she frequently visits local galleries, Smithsonian exhibitions, and attends private studio tours. She paints watercolors in a quiet corner of her home, often drawing inspiration from Mexican folk motifs. Cooking is a creative outlet - she experiments with regional Mexican dishes and modern fusion recipes for family gatherings. To counterbalance stress, she practices solitary yoga and guided meditation, and tends a small herb garden on her patio. Travel to Mexico is a yearly ritual, allowing her to reconnect with family and discover artisanal markets. She reads industry reports, technology trends, and psychology books, and occasionally participates in a small-group book club focused on nonfiction. Volunteering, she mentors middle-school girls in a STEM after-school program, leveraging her technical background while staying within a comfortable, one-on-one setting.
info.sports_persona: Isabella Saldana stays active by practicing solitary yoga at sunrise and participating in a weekly senior tennis league at the community center, while cheering on the Washington Capitals in hockey and the DC United soccer team, reflecting a preference for low-impact, socially selective exercise paired with loyal support for local professional clubs.
info.arts_persona: Isabella Saldana cultivates a deep connection to visual arts by attending Smithsonian American Art Museum exhibitions, private studio tours featuring contemporary folk artists such as Carmen Lomas Garza and Diego Rivera's protégés, and collecting limited-edition prints that inspire their watercolor paintings of vibrant folk motifs, a hobby that reinforces their curiosity and appreciation for nuanced storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Isabella Saldana's travel style blends structured itineraries with spontaneous market visits, as evidenced by their annual pilgrimage to Oaxaca's artesanal bazaars, a recent cultural immersion in Kyoto's historic tea houses, and a planned road trip along the Pacific Coast to explore boutique galleries, all balanced against family obligations and a disciplined budgeting approach.
info.culinary_persona: Isabella Saldana experiments in the kitchen with regional dishes like mole negro and chiles en nogada, frequently reimagining them through modern twists such as quinoa-infused tamales or kimchi-scented birria tacos, while their herb garden supplies fresh cilantro, epazote, and lime zest to elevate each recipe, showcasing a cooking skill level that borders on professional hobbyist.
